## Natural history notes

A small treehopper characterized by a wedge-shaped body and an enlarged, helmet-like pronotum that forms a sloped or slightly falcate ridge over the back. In Florida, Telamona subfalcata has been collected in northern and central parts of the state and has been recorded from hackberry, so it is most likely found in hardwood edges, hammocks, parks, yards, and forest margins where Celtis and other woody hosts occur. Adults and nymphs feed by piercing plant tissue and drinking sap, while also producing honeydew and serving as prey for spiders, assassin bugs, birds, and parasitoid wasps.
